newsitem.title: GERMANY: No automatic Tchibo/Eduscho deal - cartel office.
newsitem.headline: No automatic Tchibo/Eduscho deal - cartel office.

text.p: There will not be automatic approval of the planned purchase of Bremen coffee roaster Eduscho by competitor Tchibo, head of the German federal cartel office, Dieter Wolf was quoted as saying.
A cartel office spokeswoman said Wolf made the remark during discussions with journalists on Thursday.
The office had not yet received a formal application, but was expecting the papers to arrive next week, she said.
Under the proposed purchase, Tchibo Holding AG in Hamburg would buy Eduscho GmbH & Co KG, effective January 1.
Eduscho owner Rolf Schopf has put the possible sales price at 200 million marks.
The spokeswoman said the office would look into joint sales values of the two companies, their future position, and the competitive environment.
Eduscho has said its volume market shares in the roasted coffee market are 11 percent while Tchibo's is above 19 percent.
The two companies would be probably be battling with Kraft Jacobs Suchard, currently accounting for 30.7 percent in volume sales, for market leadership, analysts said.
Germany is the world's second largest coffee consumer after the U.S. and likely to keep green coffee equivalent consumption steady at last year's 564,000 tonnes in 1996.
Joint sales values would be boosted by the fact that their premium coffee products are priced above the market average.
Once the papers have been received, the cartel office has up to four months to reach a decision.
